title: nvlib-path-shim-journal - commands and hypotheses
content:
Quick journal: chasing weird library/driver shadowing that makes some inference jobs OOM at startup. Not a full postmortem, this is my scratchpad for commands I ran, short error snippets, and hypotheses so I don't forget edge cases.

High-level symptom:
- Some containers (same image + model) boot fine on colossus-3a but OOM immediately on colossus-3b. Both have same driver package version reported by nvidia-smi but different OS-level ldconfig setup.
- Symptoms: process fails mid-init with CUDA allocation error (cudaMalloc failed) or sometimes NVML returns timeout when querying memory. Intermittent.

What I verified first (quick checks):
- nvidia-smi -a (confirm driver reported, GPU states)
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
- ldconfig -p | grep -E "libcuda|libnvidia-"
- ldd $(which python3) (just to see glibc linkage)

Commands I ran (in order) with notes:
1) docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint /bin/bash image:vX -c 'nvidia-smi; env | grep -i nvidia; ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu | egrep "nvidia|cuda|nvml"'
   - Observed: on failing host there is a /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> libcuda.so.1 symlink to a vendor-installed path (/opt/nvidia/lib/libcuda.so.1) AND a local /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so present in image. Potential double-source.

2) strace -e openat -f python -c 'import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL("libcuda.so.1")' 2>&1 | egrep "openat|ENOENT"
   - Observed: loader opens /etc/ld.so.cache -> resolves to vendor /opt path first on bad host. When I forced LD_LIBRARY_PATH to include image /usr/local/cuda/lib64 ahead, it loaded image's libcuda and behavior changed (sometimes still OOM).

3) LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so python -c 'import cupy; cupy.empty((1024,1024))'
   - Sometimes bypasses the ENOENT but then crashes with allocation error earlier in runtime. Suggests symbol/soname compatible but ABI subtle mismatch.

4) sudo ldconfig -v | egrep "cuda|nvidia"  # checked caches created by ops tooling

5) nvprof / simple cuda-memcheck quick-run inside container to see if runtime allocation path triggers driver errors

Error snippets seen: (copied raw)
- "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: out of memory"
- "E0723 11:02:45.123456 14023 gpu_allocator.cc:87] failed to allocate 2147483648 bytes: cudaMalloc returned 2"
- "NVML: Timeout while waiting for response"
- "dlopen: cannot open shared object file: /opt/nvidia/lib/libnvidia-ml.so.1: wrong ELF class: ELFCLASS32" (seen once on a test node with stray 32-bit libs)

Hypotheses (rough, prioritized):
A) Shadowed libcuda/libnvidia-ml of different build/bitness or ABI on host vs image leading to subtle failure modes (symbol mismatch vs OOM).
B) LD_CACHE vs LD_LIBRARY_PATH precedence: host ldconfig cache pointing at vendor libs that are incompatible with image's CUDA runtime. The runtime ends up using a driver build that thinks GPU memory layout differs -> allocation error.
C) NVML timeout path is separate: if driver is responding slowly (OOM + heavy driver work), NVML queries time out and higher-level runtime treats as fatal. This could present as intermittent.
D) File permissions / stale mount race: if image expects /dev/nvidia-ctl ready earlier than host sets it up, some initial probes fail and runtime chooses fallback path that uses more memory. (less likely)
E) 32-bit/64-bit mixing on certain nodes (ELFCLASS32 error) - mis-installed compatibility libs from earlier ops changes.

Quick experiments to run next (ordered):
- Reproduce minimal: small python program that only loads libcuda via ctypes and prints exports (nm -D) to see which symbols are resolved and exact soname loaded. Compare host vs image.
- Start container with --entrypoint /bin/bash, set LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64:/opt/nvidia/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH, run python simple allocator to see determinism. Log full env and ldd of runtime libs.
- Try wrapping with LD_DEBUG=libs to trace which libcuda is used and symbol resolution sequence.
- On failing host, move /opt/nvidia/lib/libcuda.so.1 temporarily (rename) and see if container auto-falls back to image lib. (coord with infra)
- Build a tiny repro that calls cuInit(), cuDeviceGetMemoryInfo() and prints returned values before doing allocations. Use both lib sources.
- Run with NVML logging enabled if possible, and increase driver debug verbosity.

Notes on a weird result: when I forced LD_PRELOAD to image libcuda, the process sometimes loaded the lib but then crashed with "unresolved symbol: cuCtxCreate_v2" even though nm showed symbol present. That suggests versioned symbol differences (GLIBC style versioning or SONAME mismatch) rather than simple missing symbol. So pay attention to versioned symbol tables.

Potential mitigation for production:
- For Dedicated hosts, pin a curated /opt/nvidia driver package and ensure container images do not ship their own libcuda (strip it from images at build-time).
- For Private/VPC mode, add agent that checks ldconfig cache vs container libraries and warns if multiple sources present.
- Fallback policy: restart-in-place with LD_LIBRARY_PATH forced to image lib or host lib depending on quick determinism test. But be careful: forcing a mismatch could make things worse.

Logging to capture next time:
- Full LD_DEBUG=libs with timestamped log
- ldd of all major .so used by runtime (libcudart.so, libcuda.so, libnvidia-ml.so) and their resolved paths
- /var/log/syslog and dmesg around the timestamp for OOM or driver messages (driver may log kernel messages about failed memory map)
- strace -f -e trace=open,openat (tiny repro)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Does the image-built libcuda intentionally target a different driver API level? check CUDA toolkit minor version and driver compatibility matrix.
- Confirm whether ops recently rolled any 32-bit compatibility packages on colossus-3b (there's a note in infra slack).
- If this is widespread, we should add a CI smoke test that verifies container + host libcuda compatibility before routing jobs there.

Quick copy-paste commands for next run: (use as checklist)
- docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint /bin/bash image:vX -c 'env; date; ldconfig -p | egrep "nvidia|cuda"; ls -l /opt/nvidia /usr/local/cuda/lib64; ldd /usr/local/bin/our-runtime | egrep "cuda|nvidia|nvml"'
- docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint /bin/bash image:vX -c 'LD_DEBUG=libs python -c "import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL(\"libcuda.so.1\")" 2>&1 | tee /tmp/lddbg.txt'
- on host: sudo mv /opt/nvidia/lib/libcuda.so.1 /opt/nvidia/lib/libcuda.so.1.bak && run small repro (coord with infra)

Final quick note to self: this is messy because there are three different "domains" for libraries: host vendor libs, image-supplied libs, and compatibility/32-bit packs. Our runtime should avoid bundling driver-level libs in images. But until infra enforces that, we need deterministic detection and a safe fallback.

End of scratchpad.
